A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Deep Signature research. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B can be matched reliably; v2 additionally contains Appendix C. No material reading gaps remain.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on gene regulatory, EGFR, and GPCR dynamics, together with scalability tests, ablations, and molecular case analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and reports additional GraphTrans comparisons and parameter-sensitivity experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 retain the spectral clustering, log-signature extraction, LSTM, classifier, and three-term training objective. GraphTrans is an added comparator; the parameter sweeps test existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same gene regulatory, EGFR drug-sensitivity, and GPCR activation tasks. The added sensitivity tests reuse these datasets. GPCR atom selection changes preprocessing within retained coverage, rather than adding a dataset or task.

E2.justification: v2 adds the Transformer-based GraphTrans comparator to Tables 1, 2, and 4 and the scalability comparisons in Figure 4. Existing comparators remain. The newly cited DSR method is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 changes the stated GPCR selection from Cα atoms to backbone atoms. Appendix C introduces coarsening levels of 100, 50, 30, 10, and 5 and loss-weight sweeps over 10, 1, 0.1, and 0.01. Existing cross-validation and training budgets remain unchanged; the revised atom-selection statement does not itself establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's scalability tests, component ablations, and qualitative analyses, v2 adds systematic sensitivity studies of coarsening on both EGFR and GPCR and of all three loss weights. Appendix C and Tables 5–8 substantially expand evidence about dependence on parameter choices.

E5.justification: v1's Tables 1–4 report point estimates; v2 adds ± uncertainty entries throughout these tables and the new sensitivity tables. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting. The five-run statement and five-fold procedure are retained, without a documented increase in runs or an explicit definition of the ± statistic.

E6.justification: v2 adds GraphTrans and sensitivity results and revises existing scores. In Table 2, Cα-dihedral accuracy changes from 61.333% to 63.73%, and Deep Signature recall from 22.0% to 21.27%. Table 4 replaces GPCR results, including Deep Signature's 64.200% accuracy and 41.3% recall with 58.00% and 43.30%. Changed atom selection prevents treating this as a same-setting performance decline. Section 4.3 still quotes the old values.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix A retain the same symmetry arguments, assumptions, and time-reparameterization theorem and proof. Equation 10 corrects a misplaced parenthesis without substantively changing the mathematical definition or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient characterization of molecular interactions, symmetry properties, and superior performance on three benchmarks. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds interpretations concerning robustness to moderate coarsening and loss-weight variation, while acknowledging performance drops at extreme choices. Existing explanations of molecular interactions, generalization, and component behavior remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and a project repository address in the abstract, providing access information absent from v1. Appendix B retains the existing implementation and training details. Repository availability or contents cannot be verified from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Sun et al. (2023), DSR, and briefly positions its implicit protein-surface representation relative to interatomic pathway modeling. The remaining research positioning is substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized related-work and introductory wording edits, adds acknowledgments and Appendix C, and introduces the conference-publication header. The main section order and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 4 accommodate GraphTrans, existing tables add uncertainty entries and display recall on a percentage scale, and Figure 4 adds GraphTrans curves and legends. Four compact sensitivity tables are added. Other figures and the overall visual organization are retained.

improvement.justification: The added Transformer comparison and parameter sweeps provide useful checks of comparative performance and dependence on parameter choices that v1 lacked. Uncertainty entries and code-access information also improve transparency. These gains are limited by undefined ± notation and unreconciled prose: Section 4.3 still reports 64.200% GPCR accuracy despite Table 4 reporting 58.00%. Overall, empirical scrutiny improves, but reporting inconsistencies prevent a stronger assessment.
